title: QUIC protocol error with Chrome-based browsers
body: On our development environment with QUIC enabled, images regularly fail in Chromium-based browsers with `net::ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR 200`. After this happens, the browser may refuse to use QUIC with our origin for a while. The best reproducer is to start Chromium while forcing QUIC for the origin, open a page containing many images, switch to the grid view so larger thumbnails load, and paginate until it occurs, usually within one or two pages. Plain HTML and smaller payloads do not trigger it as regularly. I included QUIC traces, the relevant HAProxy configuration, and `haproxy -vv` output. The affected build is HAProxy 2.8-dev1-86aac23 with an HTTP/3 QUIC bind using `allow-0rtt` and `shards by-thread`.

symptoms_visible: Images regularly fail in Chromium with `net::ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR 200`, usually after one or two pages of large grid thumbnails.
After enough failures, Chromium temporarily stops using QUIC for the origin.
N0.label: N0 Chromium QUIC image failures reported

symptoms_visible: The image failures still occur while the browser remains open, and the trace contains two apparent events around 09:26–09:29.
N1.label: N1 complete QUIC trace supplied

symptoms_visible: The same QUIC protocol errors still occur with the first candidate build.
HAProxy logs the affected requests at error level even though their displayed status is 200.
N2_x.label: N2_x first candidate build still fails

symptoms_visible: The Chromium image requests continue to fail while QUIC, qmux, and HTTP/3 developer tracing are enabled.
N3.label: N3 combined protocol and mux traces collected

symptoms_visible: With the attached mux candidate, errors fall from about one per 30 images to about one per 150 images, but some requests stall for 4–10 seconds.
After the stalls and protocol errors, Chromium retries requests and eventually falls back from HTTP/3 to HTTP/2.
The development load balancer shows no CPU, memory, or external UDP-error pressure.
N4_x.label: N4_x mux candidate improves frequency but does not resolve

symptoms_visible: One updated candidate starts showing reported QUIC handshake failures within the first 11 image requests.
The other handles roughly 220 fetches before 5-second stalls appear, followed by the same reported handshake failures.
The local proxy reproducer triggers QUIC problems in about half of Chromium sessions, while other sessions work flawlessly.
The production symptom still occurs less often than before, with a couple of end-user reports per day.
N5.label: N5 updated candidates fail and local reproducer supplied

symptoms_visible: After testing a build containing the two final fixes, my previous development-environment reproducer no longer triggers the QUIC image failures.
I cannot confirm every intermittent production case because longer-term monitoring is limited to user complaints.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal development reproducer fixed

question_patterns: Can you provide an unfiltered trace rather than grepping only timestamped lines?
Were any transport-parameter lines removed from the trace, and can you capture another event without closing the browser?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I originally ran `haring -f haproxy-quic | grep 'T11:17'`, but it turns out some lines are not time-prefixed. I captured the ring without filtering and did not close the browser. There should be two events around 09:26–09:27 and 09:29, and I uploaded the raw haring-format file.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The unfiltered trace shows that the browser was closed immediately before every connection ended, and I cannot reproduce a failure while it remains open.
The same two events are present, but the capture starts several minutes earlier and includes more unrelated connections.

edges.comment: Messages c0 and c2-c5, on the reporter's HAProxy development environment: participant1 noticed missing transport-parameter output, and the reporter supplied an unfiltered ring capture after discovering that multiline records defeated the original grep.

question_patterns: Can you test the candidate build from the linked change and report whether the image failures still occur?
Please deploy this candidate on the development environment and repeat the Chromium image-grid test.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Unfortunately it still happens. I uploaded another trace from the failed run.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I paginated through thousands of images with the candidate build and could no longer reproduce any error or fallback.

edges.comment: Messages c1-c6, reporter's dev environment: participant1 supplied the first candidate change concerning STOP_SENDING on an HTTP/3 control stream. The reporter's pre-landing candidate-build test is modeled as a measurement; its raw result was that the same failure remained.

question_patterns: Can you enable qmux and HTTP/3 developer tracing alongside the existing QUIC trace and reproduce the failure again?
Please collect a new ring capture with the mux and application-layer trace sources enabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled the requested qmux and h3 developer traces with the QUIC trace and uploaded the resulting capture.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Enabling the additional trace sources prevents the problem entirely, and I cannot capture a failing request.
I captured the same failure with the trace sink set to stdout rather than the shared-memory ring.

edges.comment: Messages c7-c13, reporter's system: participant1 requested qmux and h3 traces, the reporter enabled them and returned the capture, and maintainers observed stream-control activity in the combined evidence.

question_patterns: Can you test the attached mux candidate on the current master tip and compare its behavior with the unpatched build?
Please repeat the image test with the attached candidate and report the error frequency and any other changed behavior.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the patch, the errors are much less frequent: about once every 150 images instead of once every 30. However, some requests now stall for 4–5 seconds before going through, at roughly the rate where they previously failed. I uploaded the traces.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patch has no effect at all: the rate remains about one failure per 30 images, with no new stalls.
The errors drop to roughly one per 130 images rather than one per 150, with the same multi-second stalls.

question_patterns: After the remaining errors and stalls, does Chromium still stop using HTTP/3?
Can you check the browser network panel to see whether the connection falls back after the stalls?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The network panel clearly shows batches of requests stalling for about 10 seconds, then QUIC protocol errors and retries, followed by a regression to H2. On one run the first page was fine, the second had three stalled requests, the third had ten, and all 32 requests on the fourth page stalled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. The occasional request is slower, but Chromium remains on HTTP/3 and no protocol error or retry appears.

question_patterns: Is the development load balancer under CPU, memory, or UDP pressure when this happens?
Can you share system and UDP statistics from the affected load balancer?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This is a nearly idle development VM. Its CPU and UDP statistics show no CPU or memory pressure and no UDP errors outside QUIC.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failures coincide with CPU saturation and rapidly increasing UDP receive-buffer errors on the load balancer.

edges.comment: Messages c14-c25, all describing the reporter's dev load balancer: participant2 supplied an experimental mux patch and requested minimal-verbosity traces. The reporter's candidate-build measurement showed a strong frequency reduction but persistent stalls, errors, and HTTP/2 fallback; the reporter also supplied host and UDP statistics.

question_patterns: Can you test the first candidate against the updated master build and share the result?
Please try the first requested build combination and capture what Chromium reports.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Option 1 failed almost immediately. Chromium reported QUIC handshake failures within the first 11 requests, including small images that did not fail before. I uploaded the trace and noted that the relevant part is near the end because the 128 MB ring retains older entries.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Option 1 runs cleanly for several thousand image requests without stalls, protocol errors, handshake failures, or fallback.

question_patterns: Can you also test the second candidate build combination and report whether it behaves differently?
Please try the refined candidate and capture any stalls or connection failures.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Option 2 started well with about 220 good fetches. Then one or two requests stalled for around five seconds, and the next page showed the same reported handshake failures as option 1. I uploaded the traces.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Option 2 consistently fixes the problem and does not introduce stalls or handshake failures.
The first stalls appear after about 250 successful fetches instead of 220, followed by the same failures.

question_patterns: Can you provide a locally usable reproducer or configuration that triggers the issue outside your normal deployment?
Please share the smallest setup you can use to reproduce the Chromium behavior locally.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I shared a hacky HAProxy configuration that proxies our development site through local HAProxy. It requires `/etc/hosts` changes and Chromium flags forcing HTTP/3 for localhost and our origins. It triggers QUIC problems in roughly 50% of Chrome sessions: sometimes images fail, sometimes the session breaks entirely, and sometimes everything works flawlessly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The local setup only fails when the upstream service itself returns errors; direct QUIC traffic through HAProxy remains clean.
The same local setup reproduces in about one third of sessions rather than half.

edges.comment: Messages c26-c36 and c38, reporter's candidate builds and local setup: participant2 requested tests of two updated patch combinations. The reporter ran them as temporary candidate builds, reported only observed stalls and browser errors, then produced a local proxy configuration. The later status update established that the original symptom still affected end users, albeit less frequently.

solution.intent: Apply the final pair of HAProxy QUIC/mux fixes that remove or reduce unjustified RESET_STREAM emission, then have the reporter repeat the previously failing Chromium image-grid reproducer on a build containing both fixes.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a build containing both finalized stream-reset corrections and rerun the forced-QUIC Chromium pagination test. The reporter's old development reproducer no longer failed after these changes; the fixes were subsequently backported and released through HAProxy 2.7.7.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw traces and observed how each candidate build behaved. Maintainers interpreted those traces and patch outcomes as evidence that HAProxy was emitting unjustified RESET_STREAM frames. The final accepted diagnosis is this spurious RESET_STREAM behavior, not the earlier STOP_SENDING hypothesis or the later GOAWAY speculation.

edges.comment: Messages c43-c47: participant2 announced two finalized fixes intended to remove or reduce spurious RESET_STREAM frames. The reporter tested them on the same affected development environment and reported that the previous reproducer no longer worked, while explicitly noting limited long-term monitoring. Participant2 then reported the backport and closed the issue.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted cause as HAProxy emitting spurious or unjustified RESET_STREAM frames in the QUIC/mux path, grounded in the combined traces and the behavior of the candidate builds.
Must recommend using a build containing both finalized stream-reset fixes, not treating the earlier control-stream STOP_SENDING change or either experimental mux patch as a complete resolution.

Must account for the falsified attempts: the first candidate left the original protocol errors unchanged, the next candidate only reduced their frequency while introducing stalls and HTTP/2 fallback, and the updated variants produced stalls or reported handshake failures.
Must ask the reporter to repeat the Chromium image-grid reproducer on a build containing both final fixes before declaring the reproduced case resolved.

Resolution must remain appropriately qualified: the reporter confirmed that the previous development reproducer stopped failing, but did not have comprehensive production monitoring to prove that every intermittent end-user case was eliminated.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical HAProxy operator and developer-environment administrator; comfortable building patched HAProxy versions, configuring detailed ring traces, reading network panels, collecting host metrics, and creating a local proxy reproducer.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, precise, and conversational; quickly runs requested experiments, reports quantitative differences and caveats, uploads extensive traces, and openly distinguishes observations from guesses.
